ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure is a right triangle, the bottom side is horizontal and labeled 12, the right vertical side is labeled 5, and the hypotenuse is labeled 13. The diameter of the gray semicircle is on the bottom side, the right end of the semicircle coincides with the lower right corner of the triangle, and the arc is tangent to the hypotenuse. Then reason: According to the method, set the lower left corner A=(0,0), the lower right corner B=(12,0), and the upper right corner C=(12,5). The hypotenuse AC passes through (0,0) and (12,5), and its equation is 5x-12y=0. Let the radius of the semicircle be r. Because the diameter of the semicircle is on the bottom side and the right end is at B=(12,0), the center O=(12-r,0). The arc is tangent to the hypotenuse, so the distance from the center to the hypotenuse is equal to r. The distance from point O to the line 5x-12y=0 is |5(12-r)-12·0|/sqrt(5^2+(-12)^2)=5(12-r)/13. Therefore 5(12-r)/13=r, solving gives 60-5r=13r, 18r=60, so r=10/3.
